notes:
Account summary (HelixCode):
- Devtools startup building an AI coding assistant + team knowledge search. Primary workload is streaming chat completions with tool/function calling; secondary workload is embeddings for repo/docs indexing + occasional reranking.
- Evaluating Redwood Hosted API vs Redwood Dedicated. Their hypothesis is Hosted will be fine for day-to-day, but they want Dedicated for predictable peak-hour throughput and tighter p95 control.

Current state:
- Using two external LLM API providers today with manual fallback. Complaints: cost volatility, variable tail latency during US peak hours, and inconsistent behavior across regions.
- Regions: majority NA (us-east/us-west). EU traffic starting (customers in UK/DE) but small; they asked how EU region coverage impacts latency and whether Dedicated can be region-pinned.

Key requirements / success criteria:
- Latency: p50 matters but decision will be based on p95 for streaming. Quote: "Our UX breaks when tokens pause for a second." They want stable token cadence and predictable time-to-first-token.
- Throughput: needs to handle bursty launches (product updates) and weekday peak hours. Dedicated interest is about smoothing burst pain.
- Cost: finance wants a clear $/1M tokens view and a credible plan to lower unit cost without quality regressions.
- Reliability: automated fallback (model variants/regions) is a plus; they don’t want to rebuild routing logic per vendor.
- Security: SOC 2 baseline. They asked about SSO/SAML for Console, audit logging availability, and data retention controls for logs.

Benchmark replication request (important):
- They saw the public benchmark report and want to replicate Redwood’s published latency/$ numbers using the same methodology on their side as a trust check.
- Specific asks:
  - Exact workload definitions (prefill/decode mix, context lengths, output tokens)
  - Concurrency levels + warmup procedure
  - Whether caching/batching was enabled in the published runs, and if so what policies
  - Region + hardware notes (at least at the family level) and variance/stability gates
- We should keep this aligned to the published methodology summary + any approved reproducibility artifacts. Markus to share the "how to replicate" guidance used in other benchmark walkthroughs.

POC plan (agreed outline):
1) Week 1: Hosted API trial in a prod-like replay
- HelixCode to provide sanitized traffic replay (representative prompts/tool calls; no secrets).
- Redwood to help set up routing policies (model pinning + fallback) and capture baseline metrics: p50/p95 latency, time-to-first-token, tokens/sec (contextual), $/1M tokens.

2) Week 2: Dedicated bake-off
- 48-hour window on reserved Dedicated capacity sized for their peak concurrency.
- Run the same replay, compare variance and tail latency stability vs Hosted and current provider.
- Validate operational needs: dashboards, alerting hooks, and incident response expectations.

3) Decision checkpoint (target): 2025-07-18 review call
- Present results + recommended Dedicated sizing (commit + burst) and identify if Hosted alone can meet SLOs.

Open questions / risks:
- HelixCode may treat inability to reproduce benchmark numbers as a red flag. Need to be crisp on what’s reproducible (methodology, prompts, runner settings) vs what will naturally differ (internet path, account limits, time-of-day contention) and set expectations.
- They are sensitive to any comparative claims; they asked us to keep competitor discussion "strictly data-based".

People:
- Primary buyer: Head of Engineering (evaluating cost + reliability).
- Technical evaluator: Staff ML Engineer (bench harness + traffic replay).
- Redwood: Stephanie Nguyen (owner), Markus Klein (SE).

Recommended next actions (internal):
- Provide HelixCode the approved benchmark methodology explainer + example run manifest/config (redacted) and a short note on expected variance.
- Pre-size Dedicated option with 2 tiers (baseline + burst) so the bake-off has a clear price frame.
- Send security FAQ + confirm SSO/SAML availability and audit log retention options.
